values: Evidence of whether chlorine was used within the treatment plant during each relevant monitoring period
Permit pollutant table entry for Total Residual Chlorine (Daily frequency, 19 µg/L instantaneous maximum grab) and footnote *5 conditioning monitoring and limit application on periods of chlorine use

grounding.detail: Page: 5 / Section: part_i / footnote *5 — establishes that TRC monitoring and the instantaneous maximum limit apply only during periods when chlorine is used within the treatment plant
adjacent pages around 5 — pollutant table lists Total Residual Chlorine at Daily / 19 ug/L Instantaneous Grab (*5)
No operational evidence in the packet establishing whether chlorine was used within the treatment plant during each relevant monitoring period

payload.rationale: Footnote *5 and the TRC table entry establish that monitoring and the 19 µg/L instantaneous maximum limitation are conditioned on periods of chlorine use within the treatment plant, not on every calendar day. However, the obligation also demands evidence of actual chlorine use during each relevant monitoring period, and the packet contains only permit text—no facility operational or monitoring-period records identifying when chlorine was or was not used. Without that per-period evidence, applicability of TRC monitoring and the effluent limitation cannot be established for specific monitoring periods during non-chlorine-use intervals. The permit conditioning language is present, but the operational fact pattern needed to apply it is absent; uncertainty is preferred over inferring unconditional daily requirements from the table frequency alone or inferring non-applicability from the UV disinfection statement without period-specific use evidence.
